power.shortSummary: The Trapper gathers, sets, and resets Bear Traps to immobilize Survivors who step into them. A caught healthy Survivor is injured, and the Trapper can lift a caught Survivor directly onto his shoulder. Remember the trap supply and carry limit, plus the base set, disarm, escape, and rescue timings when reviewing Add-ons.
power.fullExplanation: The Trapper starts with two Bear Traps equipped; eight additional disarmed traps spawn around the environment. He can collect traps and carry up to two at once. He sets a carried trap or resets a disarmed trap in place. The full setting animation lasts 2.5 seconds and consists of a 0.5-second crouch, 1.5-second active setting phase, and 0.5-second stand. Setting or resetting a trap grants 7.5% Haste for five seconds; sequential placements do not stack that Haste. The Trapper always sees the auras of his placed Bear Traps. An armed trap immobilizes a Survivor who steps into it and injures them if healthy. The Survivor can attempt to escape, another Survivor can rescue them, or The Trapper can directly lift the trapped Survivor onto his shoulder. Base Bear Traps cannot be sabotaged. The Trapper can also be caught in his own traps, subject to a three-second post-setting grace period; if he triggers his own trap while carrying a Survivor, that Survivor is released.

power.shortSummary: The Wraith rings the Wailing Bell to move between a cloaked state and an uncloaked state. While cloaked, he moves faster and is Undetectable, but cannot attack Survivors; uncloaking takes time and is followed by a short speed burst. Add-ons can adjust the cloak cycle, cloaked movement, sound cues, and information or effects gained from attacks.
power.fullExplanation: The Wraith starts a Trial cloaked. In this state he is Undetectable, moves at 6 m/s, and is fully invisible to Survivors beyond 20 metres; within 20 metres, he is partially visible. If stationary long enough, he becomes fully transparent while he remains still. He cannot attack Survivors while cloaked, but can interact with Props, temporarily revealing only the parts of his body needed for those interactions. Beginning to cloak produces a rattling audio cue. Cloaking takes 1.5 seconds at 4.6 m/s. Holding the Power button while cloaked rings the Wailing Bell and begins the three-second uncloak action. After uncloaking, he receives a one-second boost to 6.9 m/s, equal to 150% of his normal 4.6 m/s speed; a Lunge Attack during that boost reaches 10.35 m/s. Bell toll and transition whoosh have separate audible ranges. Surprise Attack is a score event for a Basic Attack shortly after uncloaking, not a Special Attack.

power.shortSummary: The Hillbilly charges his Chainsaw and launches into a fast Chainsaw Sprint that can instantly down Survivors on a hit. Revving and sprinting charge the Overdrive Meter; when full, Overdrive temporarily increases sprint speed, charge speed, and cooldown recovery. Add-ons can change Chainsaw handling, charge, cooldown, and Overdrive behavior.
power.fullExplanation: Holding the Power button charges the Chainsaw; releasing at full charge launches The Hillbilly into a Chainsaw Sprint. During the sprint he moves at 10.12 m/s. The first second uses a high 412 degrees/second turn rate, after which the turn rate falls to 32 degrees/second. A Survivor hit by the Chainsaw loses two health states. Chainsaw outcomes have different base cooldowns: 2.7 seconds after a Survivor hit, 2.5 seconds after an obstacle collision, 2.7 seconds after a miss, and one second after breaking a dropped Pallet or Breakable Wall. Revving and sprinting build the Overdrive Meter at 1.5 charges per second; revving has a 0.5-second buffer before it contributes. The meter activates Overdrive at 20 charges. If Chainsaw use stops, the meter waits eight seconds and then loses one charge per second. Overdrive lasts 20 seconds, raises Sprint speed to 12 m/s, increases Chainsaw charge speed by 5%, and reduces Chainsaw cooldown by 10%. Transitioning between normal and Overdrive Sprint speed takes one second.

power.shortSummary: The Nurse charges Blinks to teleport through walls and other obstacles. She starts with two Blink charges and can Chain Blink during a short window after the first Blink; after the sequence, she enters Fatigue. Charge, range, recharge, and Fatigue are distinct mechanics, and an attack after Blinking is a Special Attack.
power.fullExplanation: The Nurse begins with two Blink Tokens. Holding the Power button charges a Blink; releasing it initiates the teleport. A Blink has a base minimum range of 1.5 metres, and a fully charged first Blink can travel up to 20 metres through walls, obstacles, and between floors. Blink travel duration scales from 0.25 to 1.5 seconds. After the first Blink, a 1.5-second Chain Blink window opens if a Token remains; a Chain Blink can travel up to 12 metres. When the window closes or the final chain ends, The Nurse enters Fatigue. Fatigue is two seconds after one Blink, with an additional 0.5 seconds per extra Blink; using a Blink Attack adds one second. The base kit has two Tokens, so a three-Blink fatigue example is Add-on-dependent. Blink Tokens recharge one at a time at three seconds per charge, beginning during Fatigue. The Nurse cannot be stunned during Fatigue. An attack performed after Blinking and before Fatigue is a Blink Attack classified as a Special Attack.

power.shortSummary: The Shape's Evil Within uses three switchable modes: Stalker, Pursuer, and Evil Incarnate. Stalker Mode lets him stalk Survivors to fill a meter; a full meter unlocks Evil Incarnate, which grants Slaughtering Strike and a close-range kill interaction against eligible Survivors. Current base Evil Within does not make all Survivors Exposed.
power.fullExplanation: The Shape can switch between Stalker Mode and Pursuer Mode. Stalker Mode is slower, grants Undetectable, and enables Stalking. Holding the Power button highlights Survivors in range and fills the Stalk Meter from the closest highlighted Survivor. Stalking while moving is slower than stationary stalking. If the meter is above 50% but not full and The Shape goes 20 seconds without Stalking, it decays at 1 Stalk Point per second until it reaches 50%. Filling the meter immediately changes Stalker Mode to Pursuer Mode and leaves Stalker Mode unavailable while the meter remains full. From Pursuer Mode, The Shape can activate Evil Incarnate in a 2-second interaction. Evil Incarnate lasts 60 seconds and grants Slaughtering Strike, a charged lunge that can down healthy Survivors and break dropped Pallets or Breakable Walls. If Evil Incarnate reaches 0 while Slaughtering Strike is already being charged, the mode can linger for up to 3 additional seconds so the Strike may continue charging and be initiated. In Evil Incarnate, The Shape can also perform a close-range kill interaction on Survivors who have reached two Hook Stages, subject to the Endurance restriction.

power.shortSummary: The Hag places hidden Phantasm Traps. Survivors who trigger one create a temporary Mud Phantasm that can serve as a teleport destination within 48 metres.
power.fullExplanation: The Hag starts with 10 traps. Placing another at capacity recycles the oldest. Setting a trap takes 1.9 seconds total, including crouching, drawing, and standing. A Survivor entering its 2.7-metre trigger area creates a Mud Phantasm that turns their camera toward it and emits a fake 8-metre Terror Radius. Survivors can avoid triggering it by crouching or interacting with a Prop, or remove it with a 4-second crouched wipe-away interaction. The Hag can teleport to a triggered trap within 48 metres while its Phantasm lasts 6 seconds.

power.shortSummary: Shock Therapy and Static Blast build Madness. Higher Madness tiers disrupt Skill Checks, create hallucinations and screams, and restrict many Survivor actions until Snap Out of It is completed.
power.fullExplanation: Shock Therapy is a charged cone attack that adds 0.5 Madness points and suppresses interaction prompts for 2.5 seconds. Static Blast hits Survivors across the current Terror Radius, except those in Lockers, adding 1 Madness point and interrupting interactions. Madness thresholds are 1, 2, and 3 points; Madness does not decay. Tier III causes recurring screams and restricts many actions and item use. Survivors can complete the 12-second Snap Out of It interaction to reset to Tier I.

complexRules.name: Shock geometry and Locker protection
complexRules.description: Shock Therapy passes through ordinary walls/obstacles but Lockers protect occupants; substantial elevation differences can prevent the cone from connecting. Static Blast uses the current Terror Radius as a world-space range and also does not affect Survivors inside Lockers.

complexRules.name: Oblivious interaction
complexRules.description: Shock Therapy and Static Blast remove Oblivious on affected Survivors. Static Blast can still affect an Oblivious Survivor who is physically inside The Doctor's actual current Terror Radius because the Terror Radius is used as a world-space range, not a perception requirement.

complexRules.name: Snap Out of It failure
complexRules.description: Snap Out of It takes 12 seconds and has guaranteed checks at 25%, 50%, and 75%. Failing a check regresses progress to the previous checkpoint and causes the Survivor to scream; completion resets Madness to Tier I.

complexRules.name: Repeated Shock Therapy unhook interruption protection
complexRules.description: Patch 8.7.0 added a cooldown/protection against repeatedly interrupting Unhooks with Shock Therapy. This record does not extrapolate that rule to Static Blast without direct evidence.

power.shortSummary: The Cannibal uses a token-powered Chainsaw Sweep that can hit multiple Survivors. He can chain further Dashes by spending tokens; revving too long or hitting an obstacle triggers Tantrum.
power.fullExplanation: The Cannibal starts with 3 tokens, which recharge at 0.25 per second while the Chainsaw is not in use. Charging takes 2 seconds. A Sweep consumes a token and lasts 2.5 seconds; pressing the Power button again during it spends another token and resets the timer. The Sweep can hit multiple Survivors and downs healthy Survivors. Tantrum starts when the meter fills during revving or when a Sweep hits an obstacle. It removes remaining tokens, lasts 3 seconds plus 1 second per token consumed up to 6 seconds, and reduces movement speed to 0.46 m/s.

power.shortSummary: The Nightmare gradually pulls Survivors into the Dream World, switches between Dream Snares and Dream Pallets, and uses Dream Projection to teleport. Dream Pallet drops and Freddy's manually activated Rupture are separate events.
power.fullExplanation: Awake Survivors build Microsleep and enter the Dream World after 60 seconds. A Basic Attack puts an awake Survivor to sleep unless they have Alarm Clock Sleep Immunity. Sleeping Survivors are Oblivious and hear a 32-metre Lullaby. Dream Snares add 30 seconds of Microsleep to awake Survivors or Hinder sleeping Survivors by 12% for 4.5 seconds. Dream Snares and Dream Pallets are both part of the base kit and can be switched with the ability control. Freddy can place up to 8 Dream Pallets and manually activate Rupture on a placed Pallet; after 1.5 seconds the 3.5-metre Rupture adds 60 seconds of Microsleep to awake Survivors or removes one Health State from sleeping Survivors. A Survivor dropping a Dream Pallet instead destroys the illusion in a blood burst and can stun Freddy, but does not trigger Rupture. Dream Projection teleports to a Generator in any repair state or near a sleeping Survivor involved in healing; nearby Survivors are revealed by Killer Instinct for 3 seconds and awake Survivors gain 15 seconds of Microsleep.

power.shortSummary: The Pig can crouch to become Undetectable and use an Ambush Dash. She can place Reverse Bear Traps on downed Survivors; traps activate when a Generator is completed and must be removed at Jigsaw Boxes before their timer expires.
power.fullExplanation: The Pig begins with four non-replenishable Reverse Bear Traps. She attaches one to a downed Survivor. The trap is inactive until a Generator is completed; then the trap activates and its 150-second Death Timer begins. The timer pauses while its wearer is downed, hooked, or being chased by The Pig. An active trap kills its wearer if the timer expires or they attempt to leave through an Exit Gate. Survivors remove traps by searching Jigsaw Boxes. A standard Trial has five boxes and a shared pool of 12 searches across the four traps; each trap is assigned one to four searches, and the fourth search guarantees removal. Crouching grants Undetectable and removes the Terror Radius and Red Stain, while reducing movement speed. From the Crouched State, The Pig can charge and perform an Ambush Dash.

power.shortSummary: The Clown throws bottles from a shared stock, switching between Afterpiece Tonic and Afterpiece Antidote. Tonic clouds impair Survivors and hinder movement; active Antidote clouds grant Haste to players who enter them.
power.fullExplanation: The Clown carries six bottles shared between the purple Tonic and yellow Antidote. He switches types, throws bottles, and reloads the shared stock. Tonic gas intoxicates Survivors, impairing vision, causing coughing, suppressing fast vaults, and applying Hindered. Antidote creates an inactive white cloud that turns yellow after its activation delay and grants Haste to players who touch it. The two cloud types neutralize each other when they meet. Reloading takes 2.5 seconds and slows The Clown to 2.3 m/s.

power.shortSummary: The Spirit charges Yamaoka's Haunting to leave a stationary Husk and enter Phase-Walk. While phased she moves rapidly and is invisible to Survivors, but tracks them through Scratch Marks, sound, and environmental cues.
power.fullExplanation: Holding the Power button charges Yamaoka's Haunting for 1.5 seconds. The Spirit then leaves a stationary Husk and can Phase-Walk for up to five seconds at 7.04 m/s. During Phase-Walk, The Spirit and Survivors cannot see one another; she can still see Scratch Marks, hear Survivor sounds, and use environmental movement as tracking information, and she does not collide with Survivors. Survivors within 24 metres hear a directional phasing cue, while the Husk emits a 24-metre Terror Radius. After Phase-Walk ends, The Spirit retains the increased movement speed for one second and can attack immediately. The Power Gauge recharges at one-third of a charge per second after Phase-Walk ends, so a fully depleted five-charge gauge takes 15 seconds to refill.

power.shortSummary: Feral Frenzy gives The Legion a time-limited sprint, Feral Vaults, and Feral Slashes that injure Survivors and inflict Deep Wound. Successful hits refill the Power Gauge, increase movement speed, and trigger Killer Instinct on eligible nearby Survivors.
power.fullExplanation: When the Power Gauge is full, The Legion can enter Feral Frenzy for up to 11 seconds, moving at 5.2 m/s with a 40-metre Terror Radius. While active, The Legion can Feral Vault dropped Pallets and Windows and use Feral Slash. A valid Feral Slash injures the Survivor, inflicts Deep Wound, refills the gauge, increases Frenzy speed by 0.24 m/s, and triggers Killer Instinct on eligible Survivors within The Legion's current Terror Radius. After four valid chained hits the speed bonus reaches +0.96 m/s; the fifth chained Feral Slash is lethal and can down its target even if that Survivor already has Deep Wound. Before the lethal fifth hit is primed, hitting a Survivor already suffering from Deep Wound ends Frenzy, as does missing a Feral Slash. After Frenzy ends, The Legion enters Fatigue for 2.5 seconds at 2.3 m/s, while the Power Gauge has already begun recharging.

power.shortSummary: The Plague uses Vile Purge to infect Survivors and objects. Infection accumulates until Survivors become injured and Broken; they can cleanse at Pools of Devotion, which gives The Plague access to Corrupt Purge. Corrupt Purge directly damages Survivors.
power.fullExplanation: Vile Purge is a charged stream of infectious bile. Hitting a Survivor builds Sickness; hitting Survivor-interactable environmental objects infects them temporarily, and infected Survivors can spread Sickness through vomiting and interactions. When a Survivor's Sickness meter fills, they become injured and Broken until they cleanse. Cleansing at an uncorrupted Pool removes Sickness, heals the Survivor to full health, and corrupts that Pool. The Plague can drink from a corrupted Pool to replace Vile Purge with Corrupt Purge for 60 seconds; Corrupt Purge directly removes a Health State on a hit and does not apply Sickness. If The Plague is stunned during Corrupt Purge, the Power immediately resets to Vile Purge. If all Pools become corrupted, The Plague automatically gains Corrupt Purge after five seconds and all Pools reset.

power.shortSummary: Night Shroud grants Undetectable and enables individual Survivor stalking. Filling a Survivor's Stalk Meter Marks them and applies Exposed for 60 seconds. Performing a Basic Attack or being successfully revealed by a Survivor ends Night Shroud.
power.fullExplanation: Activating Night Shroud grants Undetectable and enables stalking. Each Survivor has an individual Stalk Meter. Stalking within 40 metres fills it at 22.5 points per second, doubled to 45 points per second while leaning. At 100 points, the Survivor becomes Marked and Exposed for 60 seconds and cannot reveal The Ghost Face. Survivors can reveal him while Night Shroud is active by keeping enough of his model in view for 1.5 seconds from within 32 metres; a successful reveal ends the Power and triggers Killer Instinct for 4 seconds on the revealing Survivor. Performing a Basic Attack also ends Night Shroud and empties its gauge. Crouching is a separate locomotion ability that moves at 4.0 m/s and does not itself grant Undetectable.

power.shortSummary: Of the Abyss combines Shred, a charged lunging Special Attack, with Portal travel through the Upside Down. Survivors near active Portals can be Oblivious and detected during channeling; they can seal active Portals, returning them to the Portal supply.
power.fullExplanation: The Demogorgon can place up to six Portals. Newly placed Portals are inactive, hidden from Survivors, unsealable, and have no detection area. Traversing between Portals activates both endpoints. Active Portals are visible and can be sealed; when a Survivor begins sealing one, that Portal's Aura is revealed to the other Survivors. While channeling Of the Abyss, The Demogorgon detects Survivors within an active Portal's 4-metre area with Killer Instinct, and Survivors suffer Oblivious while they remain in that area. Portal traversal grants Undetectable for 12 seconds after emerging. Survivors can seal active Portals, returning them to The Demogorgon's supply. Shred is a charged lunging Special Attack that moves at 19 m/s and can damage Survivors or break dropped Pallets and Breakable Walls. A charge below the Shred threshold results in a normal lunge.

power.shortSummary: Yamaoka's Wrath builds a Power Gauge from Blood Orbs, passive gain, and a bonus for injuring a healthy Survivor with a Basic Attack. At full charge, Blood Fury enables Demon Dash and Demon Strike.
power.fullExplanation: Injured Survivors leave Blood Orbs as they move and perform certain actions. The Oni absorbs nearby Orbs to fill Yamaoka's Wrath. The gauge also gains passively but stops at 98 charges; at least one Orb is needed to reach 100. A successful Basic Attack that injures a healthy Survivor grants 40 charges. At full charge, The Oni can enter Blood Fury, which enables Demon Dash and Demon Strike. Blood Fury drains over time; downing a Survivor removes seven seconds from the remaining duration. Picking up a downed Survivor ends Blood Fury while preserving remaining charges.

power.shortSummary: The Redeemer fires a chained harpoon up to 18 metres. The Deathslinger reels in a speared Survivor and attacks to break the chain and injure them; Survivors can struggle, and tension or environmental collision can break the chain first.
power.fullExplanation: Holding the Power input aims The Redeemer. Firing launches a chained harpoon that can spear a Survivor within 18 metres. Holding Power reels the Survivor closer; walking backward increases the effective pull while Survivor struggle and environmental obstruction add chain stress. Once the Survivor is close enough, The Deathslinger can strike with a Basic Attack, breaking the chain and applying Deep Wound as appropriate. If the chain instead breaks from stress, the Survivor escapes Injured with Deep Wound and The Deathslinger is stunned. The Redeemer holds one shot and must be reloaded after every discharge, whether the harpoon hits or misses.

power.shortSummary: The Executioner draws Torment Trails and can send a ground wave, Punishment of the Damned, while using Rites of Judgement. Survivors who cross a trail while not crouched become Tormented and are briefly revealed by Killer Instinct. A downed Tormented Survivor can be sent to a Cage of Torment, and a Tormented Survivor on their second Hook Stage can be killed with Final Judgment.
power.fullExplanation: The Executioner holds his Power input and moves to carve Torment Trails into the ground. Drawing trails consumes a finite Power gauge and slows him; stopping movement pauses the gauge. While Rites of Judgement is active, he can use Punishment of the Damned, which sends a propagating ground attack forward and can damage Survivors it touches. Survivors who cross a Torment Trail while walking or running become Tormented and trigger Killer Instinct; crouching avoids this trail interaction. Tormented Survivors remain in that state until they rescue someone from, or are rescued from, a Cage of Torment. When a Tormented Survivor is downed, The Executioner can send them directly to a Cage rather than carry them to a Hook. Cages progress Hook Stages and relocate if The Executioner remains too close. A downed Tormented Survivor who has reached the second Hook Stage can be executed on the spot with Final Judgment.

complexRules.name: Torment source and PTB conflict
complexRules.description: The 7.0.0 PTB tested applying Torment when Punishment of the Damned hit a Survivor. Behaviour Interactive explicitly reversed that PTB change before the 7.0.0 live release. Current base Torment is applied by crossing a Torment Trail while not crouched; direct Punishment hits do not apply Torment.

complexRules.name: Cage of Torment terminology
complexRules.description: Current official BHVR materials call the object a Cage of Torment. The maintained Wiki and older references call it a Cage of Atonement. The record treats these as the same Executioner cage mechanic and uses the current official term.

complexRules.name: Cage progress and relocation
complexRules.description: The Cage progresses Hook Stages. It relocates when The Executioner stays within its proximity threshold for long enough; the relocation pauses sacrifice progress.

complexRules.name: Final Judgment requirement
complexRules.description: Final Judgment requires a downed Tormented Survivor who has reached the second Hook Stage.

complexRules.name: Cage rescue protection recipient and endgame exception
complexRules.description: The protection bundle is granted to the Survivor rescued from the Cage, not the rescuer. Current 10.1.0-era protection is 10% Haste, Endurance, and Elusive for 10 seconds; Elusive is omitted once all Generators are powered.

complexRules.name: Cage versus Hook interactions
complexRules.description: Cages progress Hook Stages but are distinct from normal Hook/unhook interactions. Effects that specifically require a conventional hook or unhook generally do not trigger from Cage interactions; specific perk exceptions belong in the helper guide.

power.shortSummary: Blighted Corruption provides five Rush tokens. Rush cannot attack; a collision Slam opens a brief Chain Rush Window for a token-consuming Lethal Rush that can attack. Breaking a downed Pallet now reduces tokens and resets recharge progress.
power.fullExplanation: The Blight begins with five tokens, spending one for each Rush or Lethal Rush. A Rush lasts up to three seconds, moves at 9.2 m/s, and prevents attacks. Colliding with an obstacle causes a Slam and opens a 1.25-second Chain Rush Window. During that window he can spend another token to initiate a Lethal Rush, which permits an attack and can break a dropped Pallet or Breakable Wall. He enters Fatigue when the window closes, the final Lethal Rush ends, or he fails to Slam. Tokens recharge at two seconds each. Since 9.6.0, breaking a downed Pallet by either basic or special break sets the token count to two below maximum and resets current recharge progress.

power.shortSummary: Charlotte can release Victor and switch control between the two siblings. Victor moves quickly and can Pounce: a hit injures a healthy Survivor and attaches him, while a hit on an injured Survivor downs them. For Add-on review, the key baselines are Victor’s Pounce timing and cooldowns, the siblings’ control-switch timing, and the effects and removal rules for an attached Victor.
power.fullExplanation:
Unbinding Victor takes Charlotte into a Dormant State and gives the player control of Victor. Victor can move independently, charge a Pounce, search lockers, and be recalled to Charlotte. He automatically returns after being idle for 90 seconds; when attached to a Survivor, he returns after 20 seconds.

Victor’s Pounce charges for 0.85 seconds. Hitting a healthy Survivor injures them, attaches Victor, and returns control to Charlotte. Hitting an already injured Survivor downs them while Victor remains controlled. An attached Victor applies Broken, Incapacitated, and Oblivious, prevents locker entry and Exit Gate escape, and can trigger Killer Instinct on nearby Survivors. Charlotte can also use Victor’s Shriek while Victor is unbound: walking or running Survivors nearby trigger Killer Instinct, while crouching avoids that detection.

Survivors can crush Victor while he is idle and Charlotte has control, or briefly after Victor misses a Pounce. A Survivor can remove an attached Victor through an 8-second interaction. Victor can also search lockers; if he finds a Survivor, control returns to Charlotte while Victor holds them in the locker for up to 10 seconds.

power.shortSummary: The Trickster throws Blades that build Survivors’ Laceration Meter; reaching six charges causes a health-state loss. He gains Style Points and advances through six Style Ranks, which improve Blade throw rate and locker restocking; Main Event is available only at S-Rank. For Add-on review, track Blade supply, Laceration timing, throw rate and movement penalties, rank timing, and Main Event duration and cooldown.
power.fullExplanation:
The Trickster carries 36 Blades and throws them while in Throw State. Survivors build Laceration from Blade hits; six charges cause a health-state loss. If the Survivor avoids further hits, Laceration starts to decay after 16 seconds, then loses one charge every 4.4 seconds.

He earns Style Points through Blade-related hits, injuries, and distinct actions. Style Points advance him through E, D, C, B, A, and S-Rank. Higher ranks improve throw rate and locker restocking speed; if a rank’s combo timer expires, ranks regress. Reaching S-Rank reveals nearby Survivors with Killer Instinct for 4.4 seconds, alerts Survivors, increases his Terror Radius to 44 metres, pauses Laceration decay entirely, and enables Main Event. S-Rank lasts 66 seconds and then resets to E-Rank.

Main Event lasts 10 seconds, sets movement speed to 3.92 m/s, and increases Blade throw speed to 1.67 times the default. When Main Event ends, Showstopper has a 4-second cooldown. Style Rank is depleted to E, then can be restored up to B according to Blade hits and bonus Style earned during Main Event.

power.shortSummary: The Nemesis uses Tentacle Strike to infect Survivors and build Mutation Rate. Higher rates let the tentacle break dropped Pallets and Breakable Walls, then increase its range and the Nemesis’s movement speed while charging. Two Zombies roam the standard Trial, while Survivors can cure Contamination with limited-use Vaccines from Supply Cases.
power.fullExplanation:
Tentacle Strike is charged and then released. Hitting an uninfected Survivor applies Contamination and grants three Mutation Points, but does not itself remove a health state; it also applies 20% Hindered for two seconds. Hitting a Contaminated Survivor damages them and grants one point. Tentacle Strike can also destroy Zombies for one point.

Mutation Rate II is reached at five Contamination Points and lets Tentacle Strike break dropped Pallets and Breakable Walls. Mutation Rate III requires 15 total points, extends Tentacle Strike range to 6.5 metres, and raises movement speed while charging or holding the attack to 4.0 m/s. Contaminated Survivors are vulnerable to damage from Tentacle Strike and Zombies.

Two Zombies roam the standard Trial. Nemesis sees their auras; they track Survivors in their detection area and are attracted to Loud Noise Notifications. Supply Cases contain one-use Vaccines. A Contaminated Survivor can locate a case by aura, open it, and use the Vaccine to cure Contamination; doing so triggers Killer Instinct for Nemesis.

power.shortSummary: The Cenobite opens a Gateway and controls a Possessed Chain to bind a Survivor, slowing them and preventing them from running. Separately, the Lament Configuration charges a Chain Hunt that targets Survivors until someone picks up and solves the box. For Add-on review, the main adjustable mechanics are Gateway range and timing, Possessed Chain behavior, Chain Hunt timing, and Lament Configuration interactions.
power.fullExplanation:
The Cenobite places a Gateway 1.5–16 metres away, opens it, and possesses it for up to six seconds. While controlling the Gateway, he launches a guided Possessed Chain. A hit binds the Survivor with three chains, applies Incapacitated, and suppresses running; additional chains further reduce movement speed. Survivors can break free one chain at a time, or break a chain by moving so it collides with the environment.

The Lament Configuration appears as a map object and begins charging a Chain Hunt over 90 seconds. During a Chain Hunt, chains repeatedly target Survivors. A Survivor can pick up the box, ending active Chain Hunts on other Survivors and resetting its timer, then solve it in six seconds. While a Survivor is solving, Killer Instinct reveals them and the Cenobite can teleport to within 10–12 metres, interrupting the solve. A Survivor carrying the box is Oblivious. If the Cenobite picks up the box or downs its carrier, a Chain Hunt begins immediately; the box respawns after 10 seconds for a direct pickup and 30 seconds after the carrier is downed.

power.shortSummary: The Artist summons up to three Dire Crows, positions their Flight Paths, and launches them. Crows damage Survivors along the short Flight Path; after that they become Swarms that travel through obstacles, reveal nearby Survivors, and inflict the Murder of Crows. For Add-on review, track crow count and recharge, idle duration, projectile speed, Killer Instinct range and duration, and the Survivor’s repel interaction.
power.fullExplanation:
The Artist begins with three Tokens. Charging Birds of Torment displays a Flight Path; each attack-button press spends a Token to place a Dire Crow facing that path. The Artist can launch all available Crows along their individual paths. Crows can remain idle for up to 10 seconds, and placing another Crow resets the idle timer. A flying Crow can damage Survivors along its 7.5-metre path. After leaving that path or striking an environmental obstacle, it becomes a Swarm that travels through obstacles.

A moving Swarm triggers Killer Instinct on nearby Survivors unless they are crouching. When a Swarm reaches a Survivor, it applies the Murder of Crows. A further Crow hit on a Swarmed Survivor damages them. Survivors can repel the Murder of Crows with an eight-second interaction or remove it instantly by entering a Locker.

power.shortSummary: The Onryō switches between Manifested and Demanifested states and can teleport between powered TVs while Demanifested. Projection can add Condemned to Survivors near powered TVs; Survivors can retrieve Cursed Tapes and deliver them to reduce Condemned. Tape interactions, TV timing, visibility, and the seven-stack threshold are important Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: While Demanifested, The Onryō cannot attack Survivors and flickers in and out of view at close range. Manifestation allows her to attack and interact normally. While Demanifested, she can Project to a powered TV, turning it off temporarily and gaining a short movement-speed boost. Survivors within the area of a powered TV gain Condemned from Projection. Survivors can retrieve a Cursed Tape from a powered TV, turning that TV off. Taking the first Tape adds no Condemned; turning off another TV while already carrying a Tape adds one stack. The required destination is assigned from the farthest eligible TV, and inserting the Tape there removes three Condemned stacks. At seven stacks, a Survivor is revealed by Killer Instinct; if downed while fully Condemned, they can be killed with Inexorable Stare. Hooks lock in some Condemned progress.

power.shortSummary: The Dredge leaves a Remnant, then enters The Gloaming to move and teleport through Lockers. Nightfall builds through time and Power-related events; during Nightfall, Survivors see much less clearly while The Dredge gains Undetectable and faster teleportation. Locker teleport speed, The Gloaming cooldown, Nightfall charge, and Locker interactions are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Dredge begins with three Tokens. Activating Reign of Darkness leaves a Remnant and slows The Dredge while it enters The Gloaming, during which it cannot attack or interact with Survivors or Props. Locker auras are revealed. It can spend Tokens to teleport between Lockers, or cancel The Gloaming to return to the Remnant if the Remnant remains. The Remnant disappears after the first teleport or if a Survivor collides with it. The Dredge can remain inside a Locker and exit when desired; Survivors hear a warning after eight seconds. Survivors can lock Lockers; The Dredge prioritizes locked Lockers and takes 2.25 seconds to break out from inside. A Survivor can be trapped if they interact with a Locker occupied by The Dredge. Nightfall fills passively and faster through hooks, injuries, teleporting to the Remnant, hiding in Lockers, and having injured Survivors. At 300 charges, Nightfall lasts 60 seconds, grants Undetectable, increases teleport speed to 38 m/s, and reduces The Gloaming cooldown to four seconds.

power.shortSummary: The Mastermind uses a two-charge dash Power that can be chained into a second, longer Bound. Hitting Survivors infects them with Uroboros; infection progresses until they become Critically Infected, making Bound hits more dangerous. Charge time, recovery, chain window, infection progression, and First Aid Spray interactions are central Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
The Mastermind starts with two Virulent Bound Tokens. Charging a Bound slows him; releasing it consumes one Token and launches a high-speed dash. During the 2.5-second Chain Bound Window he can use the second, longer Bound if a Token remains. A Bound can make direct contact with a Survivor, grab them, slam them into terrain, throw them, or trigger a vault interaction, and those branches do not all resolve the same way. Critically Infected Survivors can be placed directly onto The Mastermind's shoulder when a qualifying grab-and-slam resolves. Bound interactions also apply Uroboros Infection.

Infection rises by 20 charges from a Bound and then grows passively at 0.8 charges per second while the Survivor is neither hooked nor downed. At 100 charges the Survivor becomes Critically Infected and suffers 4% Hindered until their Infection is cured. Six Supply Cases contain two-use First Aid Sprays; a 5-second Spray use removes Infection and triggers Killer Instinct for four seconds. Infected Survivors can see Supply Case auras.

power.shortSummary: The Knight creates a Patrol Path and summons one of three Guards to patrol, Hunt a detected Survivor, or carry out an Order against a Pallet, Breakable Wall, or Generator. Guard type changes patrol speed, Hunt duration, detection range, and Order speed. Patrol length, path drawing, guard-specific timings, and Hunt/Standard rules are important Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Knight enters Guard Summon mode and draws a Patrol Path. A path of at least 10 metres is required to summon a Guard to patrol; shorter paths can be used for a Guard Order. The path can reach 38 metres. A Guard summoned to patrol follows the path and may detect a Survivor, starting a Hunt. The Knight can direct a Guard to break a Pallet or Breakable Wall, or damage a Generator. The Knight can summon a different Guard while one is active, despawning the existing Guard; if the existing Guard is completing an Order, it finishes first. During a Hunt, the Guard pursues and may attack the Hunted Survivor. A Standard appears where the Survivor was detected; after it materializes and its horn sounds, the Hunted Survivor can collect it to end the Hunt and gain Haste and Endurance. Staying within eight metres of an actively Hunting Guard drains its Hunt timer three times faster.

power.shortSummary: The Skull Merchant deploys Drones that scan Survivors crossing their Scan Lines and build Lock On. At three stacks, a Survivor is Locked On, takes damage according to their health state, becomes Broken, and receives a Claw Trap that broadcasts their location to her Radar. Drone count, scan rotation and area, Lock On buildup, Claw Trap effects, cooldown, and recall-related Undetectable are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Skull Merchant starts with six Drones. She can deploy them and inspect her Radar to locate Survivors recently detected by Drones or Survivors wearing Claw Traps. A Drone sweeps its area with rotating Scan Lines. A detected Survivor gains Lock On, subject to the scan interval; standing under a Drone also builds Lock On over time. Survivors can avoid Scan Line detection while crouching or standing still. At three Lock On stacks, the Survivor becomes Locked On: a healthy Survivor is injured, an injured Survivor receives Deep Wound, the Survivor becomes Broken, and a Claw Trap is applied. The Claw Trap broadcasts the Survivor's location to the Radar for 45 seconds. Survivors can hack Drones through a minigame; a successful hack disables a Drone for 45 seconds, while a failed hack adds a Lock On stack. Recalling a Drone grants Undetectable for eight seconds.

power.shortSummary: The Singularity places and controls Biopods to tag Survivors with Temporal Slipstream, then teleports to Slipstreamed Survivors. A successful teleport starts Overclock, which improves movement and action speeds and changes how pallet stuns work. Biopod placement and targeting, Slipstream spread, Overclock, and Survivor EMP use are the main Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Singularity starts with eight Biopods and can place them around the environment. While viewing through a Biopod, it can target Survivors in range and line of sight to apply Temporal Slipstream. It can also apply Slipstream with its weapon. Slipstream can spread from an affected Survivor to nearby Survivors. A Survivor becoming Slipstreamed triggers Killer Instinct. The Singularity can then teleport to a Slipstreamed Survivor by targeting them through a controlled Biopod or firing at them directly. Teleporting starts Overclock. During Overclock, The Singularity moves faster and performs certain actions faster; pallet stuns are prevented, and an attempted pallet stun breaks the pallet. Resisting a stun ends Overclock and triggers Overheat, which slows The Singularity and prevents Biopod use. Four Supply Cases repeatedly print EMPs rather than supplying a fixed stock. EMPs remove Slipstream from nearby Survivors and disable nearby Biopods.

power.shortSummary: The Xenomorph uses Control Stations to travel through Tunnels, track nearby Survivors, and charge Crawler Mode. Crawler Mode enables a long-range Tail Strike, while Survivors can retrieve and place Remote Flame Turrets to knock it out of that mode. Tunnel detection and speed, Crawler charge, Tail Strike timing, and turret response are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Xenomorph enters the Tunnel system through Control Stations. Inside, it moves quickly, is Undetectable, and can detect Survivors moving above it within range through reddish footsteps. Tunnel travel also charges Crawler Mode. Outside the Tunnels, Crawler Mode charges passively at a slower rate. At 35 charges, the Xenomorph automatically enters Crawler Mode, reducing its Terror Radius and enabling Tail Strike. Survivors can take Remote Flame Turrets from Control Stations and deploy them. A turret with line of sight fires when the Xenomorph is in Crawler Mode and close enough; sufficient fire damage stuns it and ends Crawler Mode. The Xenomorph can exit Crawler Mode by picking up a downed Survivor. Exiting a Tunnel triggers Killer Instinct around the destination Control Station and briefly disables nearby deployed turrets.

power.shortSummary: The Good Guy enters Hidey-Ho Mode to become Undetectable and create misleading Illusory Footfalls around Survivors. During the mode, Slice & Dice provides a fast lunge, and colliding with a dropped Pallet or Window during the attack allows Scamper. Mode duration and cooldown, footfall range, Slice & Dice speed and duration, and Scamper timing are useful Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Good Guy can activate Hidey-Ho Mode for 14 seconds. During it, he is Undetectable and Illusory Footfalls appear around Survivors, producing misleading sounds and footsteps. While in Hidey-Ho Mode, he can charge and perform Slice & Dice, a fast attack that travels forward and attacks at the end or when released. During Slice & Dice, colliding with a dropped Pallet or Window allows him to Scamper under or over it. Scamper is available only during Slice & Dice. After Hidey-Ho Mode ends, its cooldown is 12 seconds under the current live values.

power.shortSummary: The Unknown charges and launches UVX, a bouncing projectile that creates a Blast Area and applies Weakened. A Blast Area damages Survivors who are already Weakened, while airborne hits apply a brief Hindered effect. Hallucinations provide teleport points and can be dispelled by Survivors, making projectile cooldown, Weakened duration, Hallucination generation, and teleport timing key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Unknown charges UVX and releases it as a bouncing projectile. On impact it creates a Blast Area: Survivors touched by the area become Weakened, and a Weakened Survivor hit by another Blast Area loses a health state. An airborne projectile can also apply a brief Hindered effect. A Survivor can remove Weakened by looking directly at The Unknown from within 25 metres for a cumulative 10 seconds; doing so reveals the Survivor's outline to The Unknown. The Unknown intermittently creates Hallucinations, with up to four existing at once. Survivors can approach and Dispel a Hallucination; a successful interaction removes it, while an interrupted or failed interaction applies Weakened and triggers Killer Instinct. The Unknown can teleport to a Hallucination at least three metres away, leaving a temporary Decoy at its starting location.

power.shortSummary: The Lich selects and casts one of four independent spells: Fly, Flight of the Damned, Dispelling Sphere, or Mage Hand. The spells provide traversal, ranged pressure, detection, Magic Item disruption, and pallet control. Spell-specific cooldowns, durations, flight range, Sphere effects, and Survivor Magic Items are important Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Lich opens Spell Selection and chooses from four spells, each with its own cooldown. Fly lets him travel over the environment and pass through dropped Pallets and Windows, but he cannot attack for 2.75 seconds after ending the spell. Flight of the Damned conjures five flying entities that pass through obstacles and damage Survivors in their path; they cannot hit crouched Survivors on level terrain. Dispelling Sphere travels through the environment, is invisible to Survivors without the relevant Magic Item, triggers Killer Instinct on contact, and disables equipped Magic Items. Mage Hand lifts a dropped Pallet or holds an upright Pallet in place, blocking its use. Six Treasure Chests spawn, but their contents are randomized and can include ordinary Items, spell-linked Magic Items, the Hand/Eye of Vecna, or the Mimic chest; Survivors can equip one Boot and one Gauntlet at a time. The rare Hand or Eye of Vecna items create a separate Recover Artefact interaction: The Lich can execute an attuned, downed Survivor who has accumulated two Hook Stages.

power.shortSummary: The Dark Lord shifts between Vampire, Wolf, and Bat forms, each with different movement and attack options. Hellfire is the Vampire form’s ranged attack; the Wolf tracks and pounces; the Bat moves quickly and teleports to dropped Pallets or Windows. Form-specific cooldowns, movement, attack timing, and Wolf Scent Orb effects are important Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Dark Lord shifts between Vampire, Wolf, and Bat Forms on a shared 3.5-second Shapeshift cooldown. Vampire Form moves at 4.6 m/s and uses Hellfire, an eight-pillar 10-metre Special Attack. Wolf Form also moves at 4.6 m/s, enhances tracking, and causes Survivors to spawn Scent Orbs. The Dark Lord sees Scent Orb auras within 12 metres; collecting one grants 4.35% Haste for 2.5 seconds and reduces Pounce cooldown. Wolf Pounce has no token resource: it performs up to two lunges with a 0.5-second adjustment window, and the second lunge is unavailable if the first hits a Survivor or breakable object. Bat Form moves at 6.5 m/s, is Undetectable with a 48-metre lullaby, cannot attack or interact with Survivors, and can teleport 2–32 metres to eligible dropped Pallets or Windows. Props can still be interacted with while shifted through the Form's interaction presentation.

power.shortSummary: The Houndmaster commands Snug to Chase a Survivor or Search along a path. A successful Chase can grab and pull a Survivor; Search can reveal nearby Survivors through Houndsense and create a path that boosts the Houndmaster’s movement. Dog vault timing, command cooldowns, Houndsense, and grab effects are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation: The Houndmaster uses two commands. Chase sends Snug along a directed path toward a Survivor; the path can be redirected, and Snug can vault obstacles while pursuing. If Snug grabs a Survivor, the dog pulls them toward the Houndmaster for up to eight seconds, subject to effects such as Endurance. The grabbed Survivor can resist and steer toward a nearby Pallet; Snug can be stunned, or another Survivor can interact to free them. A grabbed Survivor is Hindered and Incapacitated, and the Exit Gates are blocked for them during the grab and briefly after release. Search sends Snug along a directed route or to a selected object such as a Prop or completed Generator. As Snug travels, the Houndsense detection area centered on Snug expands from 2.5 to 5 metres; this is separate from Snug's 32-metre Search Lullaby. Survivors detected by Houndsense trigger the Power's tracking and injury-related effects. Base Houndsense does not grant a three-second post-effect Aura reveal; that Aura is the Spyglass Add-on. The Houndmaster gains a movement-speed boost while on or near the Search path after Snug has travelled enough distance. Snug then returns to the Houndmaster. These commands have separate timings and effects, so their cooldowns, paths, detection, and dog interactions are important base values.

power.shortSummary: The Ghoul chains Kagune Leaps into a second-Leap Grab-Attack that applies Kagune Mark and activates Enraged. Enraged raises Leap Token capacity and improves recharge, while marked Survivors and the post-mark countdown govern its duration. Current Pallet-break cooldown is resolved at one Token outside Enraged and two while Enraged.
power.fullExplanation:
The Ghoul starts with two Kagune Leap Tokens. Kagune Leap charges in 0.35 seconds and targets vertical surfaces or Survivors up to 14 metres away. A Leap consumes one Token and opens a 5-second window for a second Leap if another Token is available; the Power becomes usable again only after all spent Tokens have recharged. The second Leap can perform a Grab-Attack within 3.5 metres. A successful Grab injures a healthy Survivor, applies Deep Wound and Kagune Mark, blocks the Exit Gate for five seconds after release, and activates Enraged. A Kagune-Marked Survivor can still be grabbed; that Grab does not injure them again, but its other effects still apply. Marks are removed by fully Mending or entering the Dying State.

Enraged raises the Token cap from two to three and improves recharge from 4 to 2.5 seconds per Token. It persists while a Kagune Mark remains; after the final Mark is removed, a 40-second countdown begins, and a perfect Grab timing input adds 10 seconds while a failed input has no extra penalty. Breaking a Pallet while Kagune Leap is not already cooling down forces cooldown equal to one Token outside Enraged or two Tokens during Enraged. The 0.5-second, 50% Hindered rule applies to the affected Survivor after specific grasp-escape or targeted Leap-Vault interactions; it is not a Ghoul-side Pallet-stun penalty.

power.shortSummary: The Animatronic throws a Fire Axe that damages Survivors and embeds only when a Healthy Survivor is struck, or creates tracking effects when it hits the environment. He also travels between seven Security Doors while Survivors use their cameras and doors through a shared 100-charge battery system.
power.fullExplanation:
The Animatronic moves at 4.4 m/s while the Fire Axe is available and 4.6 m/s while the Axe is embedded/unavailable. He can charge and throw the Axe up to 16 metres. A direct hit always removes one Health State, but the Axe embeds in the Survivor only if they were Healthy when struck; an embedded Axe applies Broken and Oblivious until removed. Self-removal takes eight seconds and cooperative removal five. Environmental embeds create an expanding Killer-Instinct area, and the Axe becomes recallable after the current 6-second environmental or 8-second Survivor delay.

Seven Security Doors connect a map-wide travel and camera system. The Animatronic can travel through Doors regardless of the Survivor battery state and gains Undetectable during travel and for 20 seconds after exit. Survivors use cameras and Door travel from a shared 100-charge battery. Camera use drains 6 charges per second, Survivor travel costs 12 charges, passive recharge is 5 charges per second, and a depleted battery reboots for 45 seconds before returning with 50 charges. If a Fire Axe hits a Security Door, Survivor access and its camera are disabled; after the Axe is reclaimed, that disable persists for another 10 seconds, while Killer travel remains available.

power.shortSummary: The Krasue shifts between Body and Head forms. Body form can Regurgitate a Leeching Gland to spread Leeched; Head form can use Headlong Flight and Intestinal Whip, and can vault Pallets rather than break them. Leeched thresholds, form transitions, Headlong Flight charges, and Whip timing are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
The Krasue alternates between Body and Head Forms. Body Form moves at 4.6 m/s with a 32-metre Terror Radius and uses Regurgitate; its Leeching Gland can rebound and split into four homing mini-glands. A gland hit adds 100 Leeched Charges, deals no direct damage, and cannot advance a Survivor beyond Leeched I. Head Form moves at 4.8 m/s with a 40-metre Terror Radius, cannot gain Bloodlust, vaults dropped Pallets instead of breaking them, and gains Headlong Flight plus Intestinal Whip. Headlong Flight uses a 12-charge gauge, moves at 7 m/s, and exits in 1.35 seconds. Intestinal Whip charges in 0.3 seconds, uses the current 0.32-second obstruction/collision window, adds 34 Leeched Charges only up to Leeched I, and damages Survivors already at Leeched I or II.

Leeched I begins at 100 Charges and then passively progresses toward Leeched II at 1.665 charges per second. Leeched II injures a Healthy Survivor and applies Broken regardless of Health State. Hooking completely clears Leeched. Survivors can reduce Leeched with Glowing Fungus; five exist initially, up to six can be present, and consumed Fungi can be replaced after 90 seconds. Body-to-Head transitions can also spawn a Fungus when the current spacing/cap conditions are satisfied.

power.shortSummary: The First uses Vine Attack and Undergate Attack to build Worldbreaker tokens on Survivors. Once Worldbreaker activates, those attacks damage instead of adding tokens, while Survivors can use Grandfather Clocks to shorten its first phase. The Upside Down provides fast, Undetectable traversal; token thresholds, Worldbreaker timing, Undergate effects, and Mind Break conditions are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
Vine Attack charges in 0.4 seconds and creates a ground area that gives a caught Survivor one Worldbreaker Token outside Worldbreaker. The First can also enter The Upside Down, becoming Undetectable, moving at 8 m/s and phasing through Pallets, Windows and Breakable Walls; Undergate Attack exits that state and gives caught Survivors two Tokens outside Worldbreaker. Each Survivor can hold up to four Tokens. Worldbreaker activates under any of three documented conditions: a Survivor reaches 2 Tokens, reaches 4 Tokens, or a Survivor already at 4 Tokens is hit by Vine Attack or Undergate Attack. During Worldbreaker those Power attacks deal damage instead of adding Tokens.

Worldbreaker Phase One lasts 60 seconds per living Survivor and can be accelerated by four Grandfather Clocks; Phase Two lasts 50 seconds. A Survivor who has reached Hook Stage 2 and has four Worldbreaker Tokens is eligible for Mind Break. If Vine or Undergate damage would put that Survivor into the Dying State during Worldbreaker, they are suspended for 15 seconds and The First can perform the Mind Break Mini-Mori.

power.shortSummary: The Slasher enters Omnipresent Evil to move quickly, become invisible and track Survivors through Mist Clouds or Footprints. Jump Scare ends the mode by moving him to a nearby Pallet, Breakable Wall, or Window; Throwing Spikes injure and push Survivors, with Hook Spikes adding impalement effects. Stealth duration, detection range, Jump Scare recovery, Spike handling, and impalement interactions are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
Omnipresent Evil makes The Slasher invisible and Undetectable, raises movement speed to 8 m/s and lets him pass through Pallets, Windows and Breakable Walls. In this state he cannot attack Survivors, cannot see Survivors or Scratch Marks, and cannot hear Survivors except Generator-repair noise. Instead, he senses Survivors within 16 metres through Mist Clouds and Footprints; remaining crouched long enough avoids the sensing system. After two seconds, Jump Scare can target a Pallet, Window or Breakable Wall within 16 metres. Reappearing normally takes 1.5 seconds, or 4.5 seconds near a hooked Survivor; the target Pallet/Window can be Entity-blocked for four seconds, while a Breakable Wall is destroyed. Jump Scare grants 4.5454% Haste for 25 seconds and nearby Killer Instinct for four seconds.

Throwing Spikes remove one Health State and push Survivors. A pushed Survivor colliding with another Survivor can injure a Healthy teammate or inflict Deep Wound on an Injured teammate. A Healthy Survivor hit by a Hook Spike becomes Impaled and Broken until the Spike is removed; removal takes five seconds normally and applies 10% Hindered during the removal interaction. A Spike hit that puts a Survivor into the Dying State and pushes them into a wall can Pin them. A Pinned Survivor automatically unpins after eight seconds and enters the Dying State, while a teammate rescue leaves them Injured. Ten Scrap Piles provide regular Spikes; activating Omnipresent Evil replenishes depleted Scrap Piles and repairs Hooks disabled by Hook-Spike reloads.

power.shortSummary: The Judgment directs Divine Light, then casts it as a damaging column that applies Heresy. Heretics suffer special Generator Skill Checks and can Repent at Shrines; downed Heretics can be sent to Exile, which gives The Judgment Zealous and gives Survivors rescue and item interactions. Divine Light timing, curve window, Heresy, Exile hazards, Shrines, and Zealous effects are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
The Judgment controls Divine Light for up to three seconds, then casts it as a damaging column that passes through obstacles, applies Heresy and uses a 6-second cooldown. The cast delay shortens from 0.9 to 0.3 seconds as it is controlled; a near miss within 0.5 metres can reveal the Survivor with Killer Instinct for two seconds. Survivors afflicted with Heresy are Heretics. Heresy can come from a Divine Light hit or qualifying taunts, including three crouches/gestures within 10 metres or 45 seconds in an Exit Threshold. Heretics receive special Generator Skill Checks; a Good result removes 3% Generator progress. Repenting at a Shrine begins the 30-second Heresy-removal process.

Seven Shrines of Judgment spawn. A Dying Heretic can be sent to Exile, which grants a Hook Stage and drains it at Hook rate but does not trigger Hook-related Perks. When a Survivor is Exiled, the two closest Shrines activate for liberation, and other Heretics whose Heresy is not being removed are revealed by Killer Instinct for three seconds. Inside Exile, Seeds of Punishment remove three seconds of Hook-Stage progress per hit, while up to ten Exiled Souls can be collected to add 0.5 seconds each to liberation protections before all Generators are completed. Liberation returns the Survivor 8–16 metres from a Shrine and at least 32 metres from The Judgment, with one second of Divine Light immunity. Exiling a Survivor grants Zealous for 60 seconds: Divine Light is 10% larger, has 20% less cooldown, its damaging cast lasts 50% longer, and it can curve for 0.6 seconds. Curving is Zealous-only in the current post-10.1.2 server-side state.

complexRules.name: Divine Light delay and control
complexRules.description: The cast delay shortens and the damaging duration lengthens as The Judgment controls Divine Light longer; the column does not damage during its controlled phase.

complexRules.name: Heresy and Exile
complexRules.description: Heresy can be gained by a hit or taunt. A downed Heretic can be Exiled; Exile grants a Hook Stage but does not trigger Hook-related perks.

complexRules.name: Zealous curve-window source history
complexRules.description: Current behavior is a 0.6-second curve window while Zealous only. 10.1.1 raised it to 0.6 seconds; 10.1.2 briefly raised it to 0.8 and added non-Zealous curving; the September 17 server-side correction restored 0.6 and removed non-Zealous curving.

complexRules.name: Final-Hook kill
complexRules.description: A downed Heretic on final Hook Stage can be killed instead of sent to Exile; Exiling or killing a final-stage Heretic activates Zealous.

complexRules.name: Heresy representation
complexRules.description: The tracker records the documented Heretic state and its triggers/effects without asserting an undocumented Heresy stack/tier model or declaring the system definitively binary; official 10.1.0 language includes 'full Heresy' without defining numeric tiers.

complexRules.name: Exile versus Hook
complexRules.description: Exile grants and drains a Hook Stage like a Hook state but does not trigger Hook-related Perks. Liberation has its own protection and return rules.
